**Analysis date: 2026-11-27 | Asset: Ethereum USD (ETH-USD, CCC aggregate)**
*All exact price/indicator values below are cross-checked against the deterministic verification snapshot for 2026-11-27. The snapshot and the raw OHLCV feed agree on every value used here (no discrepancies to flag).*

---

| Open / High / Low | 1,687.75 / 1,744.08 / 1,640.96 |

Price sits **below every referenced average**: −3.4% under the 10 EMA, −8.9% under the Bollinger middle, −21.0% under the 200 SMA, −22.6% under the 50 SMA. That is not a pullback inside an uptrend; it is a trend that has broken down and is now trading in its own downside extension.

**Context of the decline** (all from the price feed): closing peak 2,776.47 on 2026-09-21 → 1,664.00 on 2026-11-27 = **−40.1%**. The acceleration phase began after the 2026-11-04 high close of 2,422.31 → **−31.3% in 17 sessions** (2,422.31 → 1,664.00).

---

## 2. Trend Regime — Bearish, and the Moving-Average Complex Is Rolling Over

- **50 SMA is collapsing, not flattening.** It fell from 2,556.20 (2026-10-13) to 2,151.02 (2026-11-27) — a −15.9% drop in six weeks, currently losing ~16 points per session.
- **A death cross is imminent.** The 50 SMA crossed back *above* the 200 SMA in early September (2026-09-01: 50 SMA 2,043.46 vs 200 SMA 2,027.10) — that golden cross was invalidated by the October–November breakdown. As of 2026-11-27 the gap is only **44.77 points (2.1%)**, with the 50 SMA falling ~16/day and the 200 SMA ~3.4/day. Mechanical convergence implies a **50/200 downside cross within roughly 3 sessions (~early December)** unless price rallies sharply. This matters because it is the signal many systematic and benchmarked mandates react to — it should be treated as a *forward* risk, not a lagging footnote.
- **Lower highs, in sequence, on every timeframe tested:** 2,776.47 (Sep 21) → 2,726.51 (Oct 4) → 2,534.70 (Oct 11 high close) → 2,422.31 (Nov 4) → 1,842.19 intraday (Nov 23) → 1,744.08 intraday (Nov 27). Each corrective attempt has been capped lower than the last. The 10 EMA has declined monotonically from 2,692.12 (Oct 6) to 1,722.96 — the short-term average has acted purely as resistance.
- **Long-term structure is also negative.** The 200 SMA has fallen from 3,159.16 (2026-03-22) to 2,106.25 — the secular downtrend has been in place since the spring, and ETH's 2026 range low is **1,506.51 (intraday, 2026-06-06)**.

---

## 3. Momentum — Deeply Oversold, Decelerating, but **Not** Reversed

**RSI(14) = 28.23.** The critical detail is not the single reading but the persistence: RSI has printed **below 30 for 12 consecutive sessions (2026-11-12 → 2026-11-27)**, with two capitulation-grade prints at **19.80 (Nov 14)** and **19.54 (Nov 20)**. RSI has been pinned in the 19–30 band for nearly three weeks. In a strong downtrend, "oversold" is a *condition*, not a *signal* — this is exactly the failure mode the indicator warns about, and the price record proves it: the Nov 14 RSI 19.80 was followed by five further sessions of downside.

**MACD is the only genuinely constructive development.** The histogram was negative from 2026-11-08 (−6.31) through 2026-11-25 (−2.56), and has now turned **positive: +2.05 (Nov 26) then +4.73 (Nov 27)** — a bullish MACD/signal crossover *far below the zero line*. MACD itself improved from −171.66 (Nov 21, the trough) to −149.39, and the MACD line (−149.39) remains 149 points under its neutral zone. Read precisely: **the rate of decline is slowing; the decline has not stopped.**

**No confirmed bullish divergence.** The MACD trough (Nov 21, −171.66) coincided with the price trough (intraday 1,538.60 on Nov 21), and the lowest RSI prints coincided with the lowest closes. Higher lows in RSI (19.54 → 28.23) came with *lower* closes (1,619.43 → 1,664.00 vs 1,721.08 on Nov 22), i.e. momentum recovered while price kept eroding — a *weakening* of the bounce, not a reversal setup.

---

## 4. The Six-Session Pattern: A Consolidation Under Resistance, Not a Base

Closes 2026-11-22 → 11-27: 1,721.08, 1,708.85, 1,677.69, 1,690.77, 1,687.74, 1,664.00 — a **1,664–1,721 range (3.4% wide)** sitting *below* the falling 10 EMA (1,722.96). Two features stand out:

1. **2026-11-23:** opened 1,721.08, spiked to a high of **1,842.19**, then collapsed to close at 1,708.85 on 16.11B volume — a ~134-point upper wick that rejected the entire bounce and stalled exactly at the Bollinger middle (1,826.58).
2. **2026-11-27:** opened 1,687.75, tagged 1,744.08, closed 1,664.00 — a **79.94-point upper wick** and a close below the open. The intraday range (103.12) is almost identical to ATR (103.07), confirming the volatility regime is fully priced and persistent.

Tight-range consolidation *below* declining short-term resistance inside a downtrend is a bear-flag profile. That is the working hypothesis; it is only a hypothesis until the range breaks.

**Volume does not support the bounce.** November's average daily volume is ≈12.4B; the two most recent up-attempts ran 8.35B (Nov 22) and 11.27B (Nov 24), and Nov 27's 11.85B is *below* average while price fell. By contrast, the down days 2026-11-20 (21.48B) and 2026-11-21 (18.93B) were the heaviest prints of the month — distribution is being done with more conviction than accumulation.

---

## 5. Volatility & Band Structure

- **ATR(14) = 103.07**, ≈6.2% of spot, up from ~85–95 through October (2026-10-11: 81.59) and marginally off the recent 111.71 peak (Nov 23). Volatility is elevated and slow to compress: a **1×ATR stop is 6.2%**, 1.5×ATR is ~155 points (≈9.3%), 2×ATR ~206 points. Position size must be cut accordingly — this is not a 2%-daily-range market.
- **Bollinger width = 658.49 points (39.6% of spot)** — the bands are wide, which historically follows rather than precedes the biggest moves; a *squeeze* into narrower bands has not yet occurred, so a directional resolution of the 1,664–1,721 range is more likely than a grind.
- Price is **not** pinned to the lower band: 1,664.00 sits 166.67 points (11.1%) above the 2026-11-27 lower band of 1,497.33. The band has *descended* from 2,177.59 (Nov 6) to 1,497.33 — the whole envelope is riding down with price. Notably, the lower band (1,497.33) has fallen right into the June 2026 low area (1,506.51) and the 2026-11-21 swing low (1,538.60), creating a single, highly-confluent support shelf at **1,497–1,540**.

---

## 6. Actionable Level Map (all derived from verified/tool data)

**Immediate resistance**
- 1,722.96 — 10 EMA; unbroken for six sessions. First gate; a daily close above it is the *minimum* requirement for any long-term-of-view re-entry.
- 1,744.08 — 2026-11-27 high. Breakout trigger for the counter-trend bounce.
- 1,826.58 / 1,842.19 — Bollinger middle / Nov 23 rejection high. Reclaim here would mark the first higher high since Oct 4 and neutralize the bear-flag read.

**Major resistance confluence: 2,106–2,156**
- 200 SMA 2,106.25, 50 SMA 2,151.02, Bollinger upper 2,155.82, plus the 2026-11-08/11 close zone (2,120.98 / 2,055.88). This ~50-point band is where the imminent death cross will occur *and* where the entire medium-term average stack now sits. Any rally into it should be assumed to be sold until proven otherwise.

**Support**
- 1,640.96 — today's low; first downside trip-wire.
- 1,538.60 — 2026-11-21 low; a daily close below it resumes the primary downtrend leg.
- **1,497.33 / 1,506.51 — the critical line.** Bollinger lower band plus the **2026 range low (2026-06-06 intraday 1,506.51; also 1,510.51 on 2026-06-26, 1,531.78 on 2026-06-25)**. A close below this band breaks the year's low; in the retrieved window (2025-11-01 onward) there is **no prior price reference below ~1,506**, so a break is effectively an air-pocket/price-discovery event where stops cluster and slippage risk is high. I will not fabricate a downside target below it — the honest statement is that below 1,497 there is no historical support in the available data.

---

## 7. Scenario Playbook

| Scenario | Trigger | Interpretation | Execution notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| **A. Trend continuation (base case)** | Daily close **< 1,538.60** | Lower-low attempt into the June low shelf; bear flag resolves down | Shorts only into the 1,497–1,540 confluence with hard invalidation; the confluence is *also* where late shorts get caught. Do not press through the band |
| **B. Range grind / no trade** | Price holds **1,640–1,722** | Consolidation; MACD improving but RSI still <30 | Best action is often **no action** — 103-point ATR against a 78-point range makes this a low-expectancy, high-cost zone |
| **C. Counter-trend bounce** | Daily close **> 1,744.08** with volume **> 12.4B** (November mean) | Oversold + MACD line/signal cross (histogram +4.73) finally confirmed by price | Target 1,826 (Bollinger middle), stretch 1,842. Trail with 1.5×ATR (~155 pts) |
| **D. Trend neutralization** | Reclaim and hold **1,826.58**, then 50 SMA | First higher high since Oct 4; bearish MA stack no longer valid | Only here does a medium-term long become defensible; until then, longs are counter-trend scalps, not positions |

**Bias statement:** the primary trend is **down**; the tactical momentum signal is **improving but unconfirmed**. These disagree, and the correct response is *reduced size and confirmation-gated entries*, not picking one side. A clean read: **MACD says the selling is decelerating, the moving averages say nothing has changed yet, and volume says nobody is paying up for the bounce.**

---

## 8. Why These 8 Indicators (Selection Rationale)

Chosen for complementarity in a downtrend, deliberately avoiding redundancy:

1. **close_50_sma & close_200_sma** — trend regime + the imminent death cross, the single most actionable structural event on the board.
2. **close_10_ema** — the responsive average currently capping every bounce; the fastest "has the trend changed?" test.
3. **rsi** — oversold persistence (12 sub-30 sessions) to separate "cheap" from "reversing".
4. **macd** + 5. **macdh** — absolute momentum level vs. its first derivative; the histogram caught the Nov 26 crossover two days before price could confirm it.
6. **boll_lb** — a dynamically descending band that now coincides exactly with the 2026 low, giving one high-quality support confluence.
7. **atr** — 6.2%-of-price volatility for stop placement and sizing; this is the risk-management anchor in a wide-range crypto tape.

*Excluded:* `macds` (redundant with macd/macdh), `boll`/`boll_ub` (context from the snapshot; `boll_lb` is the operative boundary here), `vwma` (volume-spike skew is material in crypto and the raw volume series is more direct).

---

## 9. Caveats

- ETH-USD is a **24/7 crypto instrument**; the series includes weekend prints with structurally lower volume (e.g. 2026-11-07 at 3.89B, 2026-11-01 at 4.88B), so volume thresholds should be compared against weekday averages, not all sessions.
- No fundamentals, on-chain data, funding rates, or positioning data are available from these tools — a crypto-specific driver set (perp funding, ETF flows, network upgrades, macro liquidity) is **unmeasured here** and can override every technical level above.
- The 50/200 death-cross timing (~3 sessions) is a mechanical extrapolation of the observed daily slopes; a sharp rally would cancel it. It is a projection, not an observation.
- All figures cited are directly supported by the tool outputs; no backtest, win-rate, or "historically this pattern leads to X" claim is being made.

---

**Sentiment report: `ETH-USD` (2026-11-20 to 2026-11-27)**

## 1. Source-by-source breakdown

### News — unavailable
The Yahoo Finance news feed returned a placeholder: `DATA_UNAVAILABLE: no configured vendor could serve get_news right now`. This means no institutional news framing, headline catalyst, or event confirmation is available for `ETH-USD` in the supplied window. This is a data gap, not a neutral sentiment signal.

### StockTwits — usable but thin; skew is bearish
StockTwits is the only substantive source. Thirty posts were fetched, of which 19 were screened as `ETH-USD`-related.

Classifier stance across all 19 on-topic posts:
- Bullish: 4
- Bearish: 7
- Neutral: 4
- Unclear: 4

User-labeled sentiment across the same feed:
- Bullish: 3, about 16%
- Bearish: 3, about 16%
- No-label: 13, about 68%

The labeled bullish/bearish split looks balanced at 3 versus 3, but the message bodies skew clearly more bearish than the tags alone. Several no-label posts describe weakness, capitulation, or failed rebounds, for example: `ETH-USD` at 1,664, down about 2.5% on the day and down about 26% in November; Bitcoin down about 23% over the same stretch; gloomy outlook; weekend going to be deadly; cooked coin; going back down; worthless trash; and frustration that the asset cannot reclaim 1,750. The strongest bearish evidence is therefore not the official label count but the underlying text.

Bullish signals are present but less developed. Examples include a user expecting another push toward 1,700, another noting dip buyers showing up, one saying they need to add this, and one speculative bullish call. However, these are relatively low-conviction and do not offset the dominant drawdown narrative.

### Reddit — unavailable
Reddit fetch failed for `r/ethereum`, `r/CryptoCurrency`, and `r/CryptoMarkets`. This is not evidence of quiet or absent discussion; it is missing data. Without Reddit, there is no way to test whether the more holder-leaning or broader crypto communities were defending a thesis, capitulating, or rotating toward narratives about relative strength against Bitcoin.

## 2. Cross-source divergences and alignments

A true cross-source divergence cannot be assessed because two of the three sources were unavailable. The main divergence is internal to StockTwits:

- **Official labels versus message tone:** the user tags show equal bullish and bearish labels, but the body text is more negative than positive.
- **Drawdown facts versus dip-buying hope:** price context and frustration dominate, while a smaller set of users frames weakness as a buying opportunity.
- **Relative weakness versus possible mean reversion:** posts note `ETH-USD` falling with Bitcoin and underperforming, yet some users expect another visit to 1,700 or later buying at lower levels such as 1.5k.

The alignment is that the most concrete sentiment evidence points lower: a large monthly drawdown, a weak daily move, emotional frustration, and a lack of confident bullish narrative.

## 3. Dominant narrative themes

1. **November capitulation for `ETH-USD`**  
   The recurring anchor is the size of the drawdown: about 26% in November, with Bitcoin down about 23% over the same period. This frames the asset as weak, not merely noisy.

2. **Failed bounce and broken support**  
   Posts mention 1,700, 1,750, and lower levels such as 1.5k. The narrative is less about a clean breakout and more about whether any bounce is durable.

3. **Relative underperformance**  
   One post explicitly complains that the asset goes down with the market but never goes up with the market. That is a high-signal bearish theme because it attacks conviction rather than just describing price.

4. **Month-end positioning pressure**  
   With only three days left in November, traders referenced month-end performance. This can amplify forced flows, tax-loss or performance-window selling, and short-term volatility, though no news confirmed institutional flow.

5. **Dip-buying is present but tentative**  
   There are signs of contrarian interest, but the language is cautious: another chance to buy lower, dip buyers showing up soon, need to add this. This is not the same as aggressive bullish conviction.

## 4. Catalysts and risks surfaced by the data

**Near-term catalysts or price drivers:**
- Month-end calendar pressure, with three days remaining in November.
- Potential reaction around the 1,664 to 1,700 area, since those levels were explicitly discussed.
- Possible short-term mean reversion if dip buyers defend 1,700 or reclaim 1,750.

**Downside risks:**
- A continuation of the November drawdown into a lower psychological level, with 1.5k mentioned as a potential buy zone.
- Weakness in `ETH-USD` relative to the broader crypto market, especially if Bitcoin also remains weak.
- Low-signal data environment because news and Reddit are unavailable, making it harder to distinguish price-driven emotion from confirmed fundamental or macro catalysts.

**Sentiment risk:**
- The sample is small: 19 on-topic StockTwits posts and only 6 user-labeled posts. This makes the read fragile.
- Many no-label posts carry bearish language, so a simple bullish/bearish tag ratio would understate negativity.
- Contrarian dip-buying could be premature if the trend remains weak into month-end.

## 5. Key sentiment signals

| Signal | Direction | Source | Supporting evidence |
|---|---|---:|---|
| Classifier stance split | Mildly bearish | StockTwits | 4 bullish versus 7 bearish, with 4 neutral and 4 unclear across 19 screened `ETH-USD` posts |
| User-labeled sentiment | Neutral-to-balanced | StockTwits | 3 bullish, 3 bearish, 13 no-label, but labels miss much of the bearish body text |
| Unlabeled message tone | Bearish | StockTwits | Posts described gloomy outlook, deadly weekend, cooked coin, going back down, worthless trash, and failure to reach 1,750 |
| Monthly performance context | Bearish | StockTwits | `ETH-USD` around 1,664, down about 2.5% on the day and down about 26% in November |
| Relative performance complaint | Bearish | StockTwits | One post says the asset goes down with the market but never goes up with the market |
| Dip-buying or accumulation talk | Mildly bullish / uncertain | StockTwits | Posts expected 1,700 again, said dip buyers showing up soon, another chance to buy 1.5k, and need to add this |
| Missing institutional news context | Data gap | News | Yahoo Finance request failed and returned no usable headlines |
| Missing community breadth | Data gap | Reddit | `r/ethereum`, `r/CryptoCurrency`, and `r/CryptoMarkets` were unavailable |

## 6. Conclusion for the trader

The available evidence supports **mild bearishness** for `ETH-USD` rather than outright confirmed bearishness. The main signal comes from StockTwits message content: November drawdown, frustration, weak relative performance, and repeated references to lower prices. A smaller contrarian cohort is looking for dips to buy, especially around 1,700, 1,750, or potentially 1.5k, but that group does not appear dominant.

Because news and Reddit are unavailable, the confidence is low. The sentiment read should be treated as a weak-to-moderate directional signal from retail social chatter, not as a standalone forecast. A trader weighing a position in `ETH-USD` should combine this sentiment evidence with price action, volume, broader crypto leadership, and any missing news catalysts before treating the bearish tone as actionable.

Critically, the prediction-market data itself is price-continuous, so it lets me reconstruct ETH-USD's trading regime with reasonable confidence even without a price feed. All ETH "levels" below are **market-implied probabilities, not observed spot prices** — a technical/pricing agent should confirm the actual level.

---

## 1. Executive Summary

ETH-USD is trading in a **deep, mature crypto drawdown with a stabilizing — not recovering — tone.** The single most informative datapoint of the week is a sharp *downside* repricing: odds of ETH dipping to $1,500 during November collapsed **-38.5pp to 10%**, and odds of a dip to $1,300 fell **-10.8pp to 1%**. Panic-selling has been de-escalated. But the crowd assigns essentially **zero probability to any upside break** ($2,300 = 1%, $2,500/$2,600/$3,100 = 0%, >$2,100 by Dec 1 = 1%). This is a **coiled, range-bound, low-conviction market**, not a capitulation and not a reversal.

Three headwinds dominate the setup:
1. **No liquidity tailwind is priced.** A Fed cut by the December 2026 meeting is at **1%**; by March 2027 only **11%**. First-cut odds don't reach coin-flip until July 2027 (54%). ETH is a long-duration, liquidity-sensitive asset facing 6–9 more months of policy restriction.
2. **Crypto has definitively lost the cross-asset race.** S&P 500 best-performer-in-2026 = **94%**, while Bitcoin = **3%** and Gold = **3%**. Risk appetite is flowing to equities, not to digital assets.
3. **Alt-beta is deteriorating.** Altcoin market cap dipping to $150B before 2027 rose to **48% (+8.0pp)** — the crowd is actively *adding* tail risk to the broader alt complex this week, even as ETH-specific downside is being unwound.

The offsetting positive: **systemic and institutional risk is fading.** US recession by end-2026 = **3%**, and Fed-independence risk collapsed (Powell out by Dec 31 = 8%, **-4pp**; Trump firing Powell = 4%). A stable macro floor supports holding spot exposure, but the "debasement trade" narrative that usually pays ETH is being **deflated**, not fueled.

**Net stance: NEUTRAL-to-NEGATIVE. Range-trade $1,500–$2,100; do not chase breakouts; no evidence supports adding duration here.**

---

## 2. ETH-USD Price Regime — Reconstructed from Market-Implied Odds

The Dec 1, 2026 bucket markets (all resolving within 4 days of report date) form a tight distribution:

| Implied ETH-USD band (Dec 1) | Probability |
|---|---|
| < $1,200 | 1% |
| $1,200–$1,300 | 3% (Dec 3) |
| $1,300–$1,400 | 2% |
| $1,500–$1,600 | 18% |
| **$1,600–$1,700** | **40%** ← modal bucket |
| **$1,700–$1,800** | **27%** |
| > $2,100 | 1% |

**Probability-weighted central value ≈ $1,650**, with **67% of probability mass in $1,600–$1,800**. Total mass above $2,100 is ~1%. This is an extraordinarily compressed 5-day expectation — implying **realized volatility is collapsing** and the market sees no catalyst before December.

**Derivable cross-check on relative value:** BTC bucket markets put Bitcoin at $58,000–$60,000 on Nov 28 (**56%**, with all adjacent buckets ≤5%). Combined with ETH's $1,600–$1,800 mode, this implies an **ETH/BTC ratio of roughly 0.028** — deeply depressed and consistent with the altcoin-cap bearishness in Section 4. ETH is underperforming BTC, and no market exists for "ETH outperforms BTC," confirming weak relative-interest.

**The week's regime shift is unmistakable.** Last week, "dip to $1,500 in November" priced at ~48.5%; it is now 10%. A -38.5pp repricing in one week means the last 7–10 days saw ETH **bounce off the lows hard enough to retire the tail risk**. Anyone still short from the panic should note the easy money has been made; anyone long should note the bounce ran out of fuel at the $1,800 ceiling, with zero follow-through priced.

---

## 3. Macro & Liquidity Backdrop (via market pricing, not FRED)

**The Fed is priced as hawkishly on hold as at any point in this cycle:**

| Event | Implied probability | 1-week change |
|---|---|---|
| Fed rate cut by Dec 2026 meeting | **1%** ($521k vol) | -0.1pp |
| Fed rate cut by Jan 2027 | 3% ($11k vol) | -0.1pp |
| Fed rate cut by Mar 2027 | 11% ($8k vol) | **-3.0pp** |
| Fed rate cut by Apr 2027 | 28% | **-5.0pp** |
| Fed rate cut by Jun 2027 | 36% | **+6.0pp** |
| Fed rate cut by Jul 2027 | 54% | **+7.0pp** |

Read the term structure carefully: **near-dated cut odds are being sold while far-dated odds are being bought.** The market is not just saying "no cuts soon" — it is actively **pushing the easing cycle further right**, out to mid-2027. For ETH-USD this is the central macro problem: the real-rate and dollar headwind has been extended by roughly two quarters versus the prior week's pricing. The most reflexive, liquidity-sensitive major asset has had its primary bull catalyst deferred into 2027.

**Growth floor is solid — which cuts both ways.** US recession by end-2026 sits at just **3%** on **$2.56M volume** (the deepest, most reliable market in this dataset), down -0.5pp. A hard landing is not priced.
